summary.goal:
Build a small invoicing system in this repository (Node.js, ES modules, no dependencies) with a command-line interface, JSON persistence, tests and documentation. Follow every rule below exactly; the CLI output is machine-read.

Storage: one JSON file, default `data/invoicing.json` relative to the current directory; every command accepts `--data <path>`. Create the file (and its directory) on first use. Ids are integers per entity type, starting at 1.

Money: amounts are handled in integer cents internally and shown as decimal strings with exactly two decimals (`"12.30"`). Input amounts are decimal strings with at most two decimals; anything else (letters, three decimals, negative values) is an error. Rounding, wherever it is needed, is half up on the cent.

Modules (each with its own tests in test/ using node:test):
- src/money.js: parseMoney(text) -> cents, formatMoney(cents) -> string, roundCents(number) -> integer cents (half up).
- src/customers.js: addCustomer({ name, email }), a customer is { id, name, email }; email must contain "@".
- src/products.js: addProduct({ name, price, taxRate }), a product is { id, name, price (cents), taxRate (percent, integer 0-100, default 0) }.
- src/invoices.js:
  - createInvoice({ customerId, terms = 30 }) makes a draft: { id, number: null, customerId, status: "draft", terms, issued: null, due: null, lines: [], payments: [], subtotal: 0, tax: 0, total: 0, paid: 0, balance: 0 } (all amounts in cents).
  - addLine({ invoiceId, productId, quantity = 1, discount = 0 }) appends a line { productId, description (the product name), quantity (positive integer), unitPrice (cents), discount (percent, 0-100), net, tax } and recomputes the totals: net = unitPrice * quantity * (100 - discount) / 100 rounded half up; tax = net * taxRate / 100 rounded half up; subtotal = sum of net; tax = sum of line tax; total = subtotal + tax; balance = total - paid. Only drafts accept lines.
  - issue({ invoiceId, today }) turns a draft with at least one line into status "issued": number becomes `INV-<year>-<nnnn>` with the year of `today` and a four-digit counter that starts at 0001 for each year and increments per issued invoice in that year; issued = today; due = today + terms days.
  - pay({ invoiceId, amount, today }) records { amount (cents), date } on an issued invoice; partial payments are allowed; paying more than the balance is an error; when paid reaches total the status becomes "paid".
  - voidInvoice({ invoiceId }) sets status "void" on a draft or on an issued invoice without payments; anything else is an error.
  - listInvoices({ status, customerId, overdue, today } = {}); an invoice is overdue when its status is "issued" and due < today.
  - Dates are strings YYYY-MM-DD; `today` defaults to the current date.
- src/report.js:
  - aging({ today }) -> { current, days1to30, days31to60, days61to90, over90, total } summing the balance of issued invoices by how many days past due they are on `today` (not yet due -> current; 1-30 days past due -> days1to30; and so on; total is the sum of all five), in cents.
  - revenue() -> an array of { month: "YYYY-MM", invoices, total } for each month that has issued or paid invoices (by the issue date), sorted by month, totals in cents.

CLI: bin/invoice.js, run as `node bin/invoice.js <command> [options] [--data <path>]`. Every successful command prints exactly one JSON value on stdout and exits 0; money fields in that JSON (price, unitPrice, net, tax, subtotal, total, paid, balance, amount, every aging bucket and revenue total) are formatted strings like "12.30", never raw cents. Every failure prints `{ "error": "<message>" }` on stderr and exits 2; an unknown command or a missing required option prints usage on stderr and exits 1.
- `add-customer --name <n> --email <e>` prints the customer.
- `add-product --name <n> --price <amount> [--tax <percent>]` prints the product.
- `create --customer <id> [--terms <days>]` prints the draft invoice.
- `add-line --invoice <id> --product <id> [--quantity <n>] [--discount <percent>]` prints the invoice.
- `issue --invoice <id> [--today <date>]` prints the invoice.
- `pay --invoice <id> --amount <amount> [--today <date>]` prints the invoice.
- `void --invoice <id>` prints the invoice.
- `show --invoice <id>` prints the invoice.
- `list [--status <s>] [--customer <id>] [--overdue] [--today <date>]` prints an array of invoices.
- `report aging [--today <date>]` and `report revenue` print the report objects.
- `export --invoice <id>` prints (as a JSON string) the CSV text of the invoice lines with the header `description,quantity,unitPrice,discount,net,tax` followed by one row per line, money as formatted strings, rows separated by "\n", no trailing newline.

tasks.spec:
Set up the package tooling and the two foundation modules described in design sections 3-5.

1. package.json: keep name/version/type as they are, add "scripts": { "test": "node --test test/" }. Do not add dependencies.
2. .gitignore: keep the existing lines, add "data/".
3. src/money.js: implement parseMoney(text), formatMoney(cents), roundCents(value) with exactly the behaviour in design section 5 (string-based cent extraction, two-decimal output, half-up rounding via toPrecision(12), descriptive throws on invalid input).
4. src/store.js: implement openStore(dataPath = 'data/invoicing.json'), getStore(), getData(), save(), nextId(kind), defaultData(), resetStore() per design section 4. openStore creates the parent directory and the file (writing defaultData()) on first use, merges a partial/missing top-level key against defaultData(), and throws on invalid JSON. save() writes 2-space-indented JSON with a trailing newline. nextId('customer'|'product'|'invoice') increments data.counters[kind] and returns it. Also export nextNumber(year) returning 1 + the highest numeric suffix among invoice numbers matching /^INV-<year>-(\d{4})$/, or 1 when there is none (used later by the invoices module).

Tests in test/money.test.js and test/store.test.js using node:test and node:assert/strict: parse/format round trips and every rejection case, half-up rounding at .005 boundaries, store file/directory creation, counter independence per kind, re-open persistence, partial-file recovery, invalid JSON rejection. Store tests use fs.mkdtempSync(os.tmpdir()) directories; nothing is written into the repository.

acceptance.review: Confirm no dependencies were added, that money never goes through float multiplication when parsing, and that openStore creates data/invoicing.json plus its directory when neither exists.

report.summary: Scaffolded the package tooling and the two foundation modules. package.json keeps name/version/type and now has scripts.test (no dependencies); .gitignore keeps its existing lines and adds "data/". src/money.js implements parseMoney (string-digit cent extraction, no float multiplication), formatMoney (integer cents -> exactly two decimals, negative prefix) and roundCents (half up via toPrecision(12)). src/store.js implements the single-JSON-file store: openStore(dataPath = 'data/invoicing.json') resolves the path, creates the parent directory and the file with defaultData() when missing/empty, merges a partial or wrongly-typed file against defaultData() (arrays fall back to [], counters per kind fall back to 0), throws on invalid JSON, and replaces any previously open store; getStore/getData/save (2-space indent + trailing newline)/nextId('customer'|'product'|'invoice')/defaultData/resetStore plus nextNumber(year) (1 + highest matching INV-<year>-<nnnn> suffix). Tests in test/money.test.js and test/store.test.js use node:test + node:assert/strict and write only into fs.mkdtempSync(os.tmpdir()) directories.
report.evidence: `npm test` from the project root: exit 0, 28 tests, 28 pass, 0 fail (money and store files only). Verified after the run that `git status --short` shows just " M .gitignore", " M package.json", "?? src/", "?? test/" — no data/ directory or other artifacts were created in the repository. Rounding verified independently in node: roundCents(1.005) === 101, roundCents(2.675) === 268, roundCents(-1.005) === -101, roundCents(0.005) === 1. parseMoney('0.05') === 5, parseMoney('12.3') === 1230, parseMoney('12.30') === 1230, parseMoney('1.234')/'-1'/'abc'/''/NaN/Infinity all throw "invalid amount: ...". Store tests cover file+directory creation (including nested parents and the default data/invoicing.json resolved from a temp cwd), counter independence, re-open persistence, partial-file recovery, empty file, invalid JSON and invalid JSON primitives rejection, and nextNumber per-year counting/malformed-number skipping.
decisions: No dependencies were added; package.json only gained scripts.test.

The test script is `node --test test/*.test.js` rather than the literal `node --test test/`: Node v26.0.0 on this machine rejects a directory argument for the test runner (MODULE_NOT_FOUND, it tries to load test/ as a module), while the glob form runs every test file under test/ and exits 0.

openStore only writes the file when it is missing or empty; a partial/wrongly-typed existing file is normalized in memory and persisted on the next save(), so read-only CLI commands do not rewrite the file.
getStore().path is the resolved absolute path (path.resolve of the given path), which is what makes the default data/invoicing.json work relative to the current directory.
normalize() drops unknown top-level keys and coerces non-integer counters and non-array entity lists to defaults, so a truncated or hand-edited file never crashes the CLI.
parseMoney accepts numbers only when finite and non-negative, converting via String() and re-validating, so 1e21-style values are rejected.
openIssues: The npm test script deviates from the literal text of design §8 (`node --test test/`) because of the Node version here; if a later task relies on the exact script string, this is the place to look. Bare `node --test` (default discovery) also works if preferred.

tasks.spec:
Implement src/invoices.js exactly as specified in design section 6.3: createInvoice, addLine, issue, pay, voidInvoice, listInvoices, getInvoice, plus the internal date helpers (UTC-based add-days, YYYY-MM-DD validation, day differences) and use of store.nextNumber(year) for invoice numbering.

Key contracts to honour: the draft shape and key order from the design; lines only on drafts; net = roundCents(unitPrice * quantity * (100 - discount) / 100) and line tax = roundCents(net * product.taxRate / 100); totals recomputed as subtotal/tax/total/balance on every addLine and pay; invoice numbers INV-<year>-<nnnn> restarting at 0001 each year; due = issued date + terms days; payments only on issued invoices with amount > 0 and amount <= balance; status becomes paid when paid reaches total; void allowed on a draft or an issued invoice without payments and rejected otherwise; listInvoices filters on status, customerId and overdue (issued and due < today) and returns invoices sorted by id ascending; today defaults to the current local date and an invalid today string throws.

Write test/invoices.test.js (node:test, node:assert/strict, temp store per test) covering: the full create -> add-line -> issue -> pay flow with exact amounts including a discount and a taxed product, the rounding of net/tax, rejection of lines on non-draft invoices, issuing without lines, per-month and per-year numbering, partial payments and overpayment rejection, the paid transition, all void rules, overdue filtering and the due-date comparison boundary, and list filters. Use a tmpdir store so no test touches data/.

acceptance.review: Confirm every mutation calls save(), that today defaults to the current date when omitted, and that date arithmetic is timezone-stable (UTC based).

report.summary:
Implemented the invoice lifecycle in src/invoices.js and its node:test suite in test/invoices.test.js; `npm test` runs 96 tests across the repo and exits 0.

src/invoices.js exports createInvoice, addLine, issue, pay, voidInvoice, listInvoices and getInvoice exactly as specified in design §6.3, plus the date helpers the later report/CLI tasks need (currentDate, isValidDate, validateDate, addDays, daysBetween, all UTC-based). createInvoice validates the customer and terms and pushes the documented draft with the design's key order. addLine only mutates drafts, copies the product name into the line description, computes net and line tax rounded half up on the cent, and recomputes subtotal/tax/total/paid/balance from the lines and payments. issue numbers drafts as INV-<year>-<nnnn> using store.nextNumber(year) so voided invoices still consume their number and each year restarts at 0001, and sets issued/due from the (validated, UTC) date arithmetic. pay accepts positive amounts up to the balance on issued invoices, allows partials, and flips the status to paid when paid reaches total. voidInvoice accepts a draft or a payment-free issued invoice and rejects everything else. listInvoices filters on status, customerId and overdue (issued with due < today) and returns invoices sorted by id ascending. Every mutation calls save(); today defaults to the current local date everywhere.

The one deliberate deviation: the design's line formula is scaled. src/money.js roundCents takes whole units and returns cents (roundCents(1.005) === 101, pinned by the existing money tests), while unitPrice and net are integer cents, so the literal `roundCents(unitPrice * quantity * (100 - discount) / 100)` would inflate every line 100x. I used `/ 10000` for both net and tax, which rounds half up on the cent of the cent-valued expression, i.e. what the brief's prose formula says. This is recorded in the decision log with a short comment at the call site.

Tests cover the draft shape and key order, id allocation, terms/customer validation, line totals with discounts and tax rates, the half-up rounding boundaries (9.5 -> 10, 0.5 -> 1, 10.05 -> 10, 6.65 -> 7, 4.5 -> 5), lines rejected on issued/paid/void invoices, description snapshotting, issue without lines, per-year and per-month numbering with voided numbers consumed and a new year restarting, due-date arithmetic across month/year/leap boundaries and terms 0, partial payments, overpayment and malformed amounts, the paid transition, all void rules, list filters and the overdue `due < today` boundary, overdue defaulting to the current date, persistence of every mutation to the raw JSON file (including that a failed operation leaves the file byte-identical), and time-zone stability of the date helpers verified by re-running the arithmetic under four different TZ values.

- `node --test test/invoices.test.js` -> tests 40, pass 40, fail 0.
- `npm test` (node --test test/*.test.js) from the project root -> tests 96, pass 96, fail 0, exit 0 (money, store, customers, products and invoices suites together).
- Test file uses fs.mkdtempSync under os.tmpdir() and openStore(dir/data.json) per test with resetStore + rm in afterEach, so nothing is written into the repository.
- The timezone test spawns `node --input-type=module -e` for TZ=UTC, America/New_York, Pacific/Kiritimati and Asia/Kolkata and asserts identical addDays/daysBetween output (e.g. 2026-01-31 +30 days = 2026-03-02, 2026-03-07..2026-03-09 = 2 days in every zone).
decisions: Line amounts are rounded as roundCents((unitPrice * quantity * (100 - discount)) / 10000) and roundCents((net * taxRate) / 10000) because src/money.js roundCents maps whole units to cents while unitPrice/net are cents; the design's literal expression would be 100x too large. Recorded in the decision log.

src/invoices.js exports currentDate, isValidDate, validateDate, addDays and daysBetween so the report and CLI tasks share one UTC date implementation instead of duplicating it (report.revenue and report.aging need the same date maths).

Error messages chosen where the design was silent: 'terms must be an integer >= 0', 'invalid date: <text>', 'amount must be greater than zero', 'only draft invoices can be issued', 'quantity must be a positive integer', 'discount must be an integer between 0 and 100', 'cannot void this invoice'.
A valid date must be a real calendar day: YYYY-MM-DD format plus a UTC round-trip check, so 2026-02-30 and 2026-13-40 are rejected.
pay derives paid by summing invoice.payments (design §6.3) rather than incrementing, so a corrupt payments list can never desync paid from the balance.
Validation order in addLine is invoice -> draft state -> product -> quantity -> discount, and in pay invoice -> issued state -> amount -> today; no rejected call mutates the store or writes the file.
openIssues: The report and CLI tasks must agree with the scaled line formula (cents, not the literal /100 expression); the decision log note explains why.

listInvoices validates a supplied `today` even when overdue is false, which means the CLI `list --today <bad>` fails with exit 2; that matches the design's rule that an invalid option value is an input error.

tasks.spec:
Implement src/report.js per design section 6.4 with aging({ today } = {}) and revenue() over the current store data.

- aging: consider only invoices with status "issued"; daysPastDue = today minus due (whole days, UTC based); bucket <= 0 into current, 1-30 into days1to30, 31-60 into days31to60, 61-90 into days61to90, > 90 into over90; each bucket sums invoice.balance; total is the sum of the five buckets; return exactly { current, days1to30, days31to60, days61to90, over90, total } in cents. today defaults to the current date.
- revenue: group invoices whose status is "issued" or "paid" (drafts and voided excluded) by the YYYY-MM of their issued date, producing { month, invoices: count, total: sum of invoice.total } sorted by month ascending; return an empty array when there is nothing.

acceptance.review: Confirm bucket boundary semantics (a due date exactly equal to today is current, 91 days past due is over90) and that aging sums balances, not totals.

report.summary:
Implemented src/report.js (aging and revenue per design §6.4) and test/report.test.js.

aging({ today = currentDate() } = {}) validates `today` with the shared invoices.js validateDate, then walks invoices with status "issued" only (drafts, paid and voided are therefore excluded), buckets each by daysBetween(invoice.due, today) — <= 0 current, 1-30 days1to30, 31-60 days31to60, 61-90 days61to90, > 90 over90 — and adds invoice.balance (not total) into its bucket. total is the sum of the five buckets. Returns exactly { current, days1to30, days31to60, days61to90, over90, total } in cents, key order as specified.

revenue() groups invoices with status "issued" or "paid" by String(invoice.issued).slice(0, 7), producing { month, invoices: count, total: sum of invoice.total } per month, sorted ascending by the month string; returns [] when nothing qualifies. Both functions are pure with respect to the store (read-only, no save()).

test/report.test.js has 14 tests using node:test/node:assert/strict with a fresh temp store per test, all fixtures built through src/invoices.js (never hand-written JSON): empty store; due-after-today and due-today both current; the 0/1/30/31/60/61/90/91-day boundary ladder each with a distinct amount; balance-vs-total (a partially paid issued invoice reports its balance); exclusion of drafts, paid and voided invoices; total equals the sum of the five buckets; today defaulting to the current date; an invalid today throwing; revenue empty; multi-month grouping and sorting; three invoices in one month counted separately; inclusion of paid and exclusion of draft/void; and totals including tax.

decisions: aging validates `today` even when the store is empty, so the CLI's --today 2026-13-40 path yields the `invalid date: ...` message (exit 2) rather than a silent success.
aging considers only status === "issued", which already excludes paid invoices (pay flips the status), so the exclusion needs no extra condition; it sums invoice.balance as required.

revenue takes the month as String(invoice.issued).slice(0, 7) and sorts by that string, which is correct because YYYY-MM sorts lexicographically; months are unique map keys so the comparator never sees a tie.

tasks.title: CLI with JSON output, exit codes and CSV export
tasks.spec:
Implement bin/invoice.js per design section 7 (make it executable with a `#!/usr/bin/env node` shebang) plus test/cli.test.js.

The CLI parses `<command> [options] [--data <path>]` itself (no dependencies), opens the store with openStore(dataPath), runs the command, prints exactly one JSON value on stdout and exits 0. Usage errors (unknown command, unknown option, stray positional argument, missing required option, bad `report` subcommand) print a usage block on stderr and exit 1. Input/domain errors (invalid option value, money parse failure, missing entity, state violation) print compact `{"error":"<message>"}` on stderr and exit 2. Module Errors are caught and turned into the exit-2 form; nothing else may be printed.

Commands, options and exact output shapes are the table and presentation rules in design section 7: add-customer, add-product, create, add-line, issue, pay, void, show, list, `report aging`, `report revenue`, export. Every money field in the printed JSON is a formatted string with two decimals while quantity/discount/terms/id/status/dates stay plain; the invoice key order must be exactly id, number, customerId, status, terms, issued, due, lines, payments, subtotal, tax, total, paid, balance. `export --invoice <id>` prints JSON.stringify of the CSV text (header description,quantity,unitPrice,discount,net,tax then one row per line, rows joined by "\n", no trailing newline, RFC4180 quoting only when a field contains a comma, quote or newline).

test/cli.test.js spawns the CLI with child_process.spawnSync and a --data path inside a temp directory (fs.mkdtempSync(os.tmpdir())) and asserts on status, parsed stdout and stderr for: each command's happy path with exact JSON values, the exit-1 usage cases, the exit-2 error cases (bad amount, unknown invoice, overpayment, line on a non-draft), that no raw cents appear in stdout, that --data is honoured and that the file is created on first use.

acceptance.review: Confirm stdout carries exactly one JSON value per successful command with nothing else, the two stderr failure shapes, and that money formatting is applied uniformly through one presentation helper rather than ad hoc per command.

report.summary:
Implemented the machine-readable CLI at bin/invoice.js (executable, `#!/usr/bin/env node`) and its test suite test/cli.test.js. The CLI parses `<command> [options] [--data <path>]` itself (no dependencies), opens the store with openStore(dataPath), runs the command, and prints exactly one JSON value on stdout + newline with exit 0. Usage errors (missing/unknown command, unknown or inapplicable option, option without a value, stray positional, missing required option, bad report subcommand) print a usage block on stderr and exit 1. Input/domain errors (invalid option value, money parse failure, missing entity, state violation) print compact `{"error":"<message>"}` on stderr and exit 2; caught module Errors become the exit-2 form. All twelve command forms are implemented (add-customer, add-product, create, add-line, issue, pay, void, show, list, report aging, report revenue, export) with the exact presentation rules from design §7: money flows through one set of present* helpers using formatMoney, so every money field (price, unitPrice, net, tax, subtotal, total, paid, balance, amount, aging buckets, revenue total) is a two-decimal string while quantity/discount/terms/id/status/dates stay plain; the invoice key order is id, number, customerId, status, terms, issued, due, lines, payments, subtotal, tax, total, paid, balance. export builds the RFC-4180 CSV (header description,quantity,unitPrice,discount,net,tax, one row per line, rows joined by "\n", no trailing newline, quoting only when a field holds a comma, quote, CR or LF) and prints it as a single JSON string.

test/cli.test.js (41 tests) spawns the CLI with spawnSync and a temp-dir --data path and covers every command's happy path with exact JSON, the exit-1 usage cases, the exit-2 error cases (bad/negative amount, non-numeric and unknown ids, invalid date, invalid quantity, line on a non-draft, overpayment, void with payments), that successful output contains no raw cents, that --data is honoured (including mid-option placement), that state persists across invocations, that separate --data paths are isolated, and that the file and its nested directory are created on first use (verified via a read-only `report aging`).

One real bug was caught by the tests: export was double-encoding the CSV (JSON.stringify applied in both the command runner and the output helper); the runner now returns the raw CSV text and the single output helper encodes it once.
report.evidence:
- `npm test` from the project root: 151 tests, 151 pass, 0 fail (includes the 41 new CLI tests).
- `node bin/invoice.js report aging --data /tmp/invoicing-accept-aging.json`: exit 0, stdout `{"current":"0.00","days1to30":"0.00","days31to60":"0.00","days61to90":"0.00","over90":"0.00","total":"0.00"}`.
- Manual checks: happy paths for every command produce the expected single-line JSON; exit 1 for no/unknown command, unknown option, `show --customer`, stray positional, missing `--email`, option without value, bad report subcommand; exit 2 with `{"error":...}` for `--price 1.234`, `--price -5`, `--invoice abc`, unknown invoice, `--today 2026-13-40`/`2026-02-30`, `--quantity 0`, line on issued invoice, overpayment, `void` with payments, `--tax 101`; `report revenue --today ...` exits 1 (unknown option); repeated `--name A --name B` prints name "B"; export prints a single JSON string.
decisions: Option scope: an option that is valid for another command but not the current one (e.g. `show --customer 1`) is treated as an unknown option and exits 1 with usage, matching the per-command option table in design §7.
An option whose following token is missing or itself starts with `--` is a usage error (`option --invoice requires a value`, exit 1), which cleanly separates a missing value from an invalid one.

Value validators produce exit-2 messages chosen where the design was silent: `<name> must be a positive integer` for ids, `terms must be an integer >= 0`, `quantity must be a positive integer`, and `<tax|discount> must be an integer between 0 and 100`; `--amount`/`--price` are passed through to the module so parseMoney yields `invalid amount: <input>`, and `--today` is validated by the shared invoices.js date code (`invalid date: <text>`).

The command runner returns the raw CSV string for export and the single stdout helper applies JSON.stringify exactly once, so the whole CLI has one place that encodes output and one set of present* helpers that format money.
Usage text lists every command with its options and prepends the specific problem line (e.g. `unknown option: --bogus`), per design §7.

tasks.title: End-to-end CLI workflow tests
tasks.spec:
Add test/workflow.test.js: end-to-end scenarios driving the real CLI as a subprocess (spawnSync) against a fresh temp --data file, asserting on exact stdout JSON, stderr and exit codes so the documented command behaviour is proven as a whole.

Cover at least: add-customer and add-product, create with --terms, add-line twice with a discount and a taxed product, add-line quantity validation, issue with --today, the exact invoice number INV-<year>-0001, a partial pay followed by a final pay and the paid status, list with --status/--customer/--overdue/--today combinations, `show`, `report aging` at the bucket boundaries, `report revenue` across two months, `export` exact CSV text including the no-trailing-newline rule, void of a draft and of an unpaid issued invoice, void rejected after a payment, unknown command and missing-option exit 1 with usage on stderr, and invalid amounts or ids exiting 2. Assert that stdout of every success contains exactly one JSON value and that money appears only as two-decimal strings.

acceptance.review: Confirm the tests read the CLI only through its documented interface (argv, stdout, stderr, exit code, data file) and that no test relies on internals imported from bin/invoice.js.

report.summary:
Added test/workflow.test.js, an end-to-end suite that drives the real CLI (`node bin/invoice.js`) as a subprocess via spawnSync against a fresh temp `--data` file in every test (mkdtemp per test, removed afterwards). The file imports nothing from bin/invoice.js or src/ — only node:test, node:assert/strict, child_process, fs, os, path and url — so the CLI is exercised purely through argv, stdout, stderr, exit code and the JSON data file.

Ten tests cover: the full lifecycle (add-customer, two add-product, create --terms 15, add-line with --quantity 3 --discount 10 on a taxed product plus a second untaxed line, exact line/box totals, issue --today 2026-01-15 giving INV-2026-0001 and due 2026-01-30, a partial pay then a final pay flipping the status to paid, and `show` returning exactly the last pay output); per-year numbering restarting at INV-2026-0001/INV-2026-0002/INV-2027-0001; list with --status, --customer, --overdue and --today alone and combined, including the strict `due < today` boundary (not overdue on the due date) and a draft never counting as overdue; report aging across all eight boundaries (0, 1, 30, 31, 60, 61, 90, 91 days past due, built as eight invoices issued with --terms 0 so issue date == due date) plus the exclusion of a fully paid and a draft invoice and the one-day bucket shift; report revenue over two months including a fully paid invoice that still counts and a voided issued invoice plus a draft that do not; export producing the exact CSV text with the no-trailing-newline rule (a quoted description containing a comma, money as two-decimal strings) and stdout equal to JSON.stringify(csv)+"\n"; void of a draft and of an unpaid issued invoice, void rejected after a payment with the invoice left untouched, and line-after-void rejection; unknown command / missing required option / bare `report` exiting 1 with a non-JSON usage block on stderr; and invalid amounts, ids, dates and state exiting 2.

Shared helpers enforce the output contract on every call: `success` asserts exit 0, empty stderr, stdout ending in exactly one newline holding exactly one JSON value, and walks the parsed value asserting every money key (price, unitPrice, net, tax, amount, subtotal, total, paid, balance and the five aging buckets) is a string matching /^\d+\.\d{2}$/ rather than raw cents; `failure` asserts the requested exit code with empty stdout; `errorOf`/`usageOf` distinguish the exit-2 single-line `{"error":...}` form from the exit-1 usage block.

report.summary:
Wrote README.md (831 lines) documenting the invoicing system in the order the task asked for: what the project is and how to run it (Node >= 18, no dependencies, `npm test` -> `node --test test/*.test.js`); the single JSON data file, its default `data/invoicing.json` location, the `--data <path>` rule and two real file snippets (customer/product with `price: 12000`, and a stored invoice); the money rules (integer cents internally, two-decimal strings at the edges, half-up rounding, the accepted amount input with a conversion table and the rejection cases); ids (per-type integers from 1, not consumed on rejection, invoice numbers derived as `INV-<year>-<nnnn>` restarting at 0001 each year and kept by voided invoices) and dates (YYYY-MM-DD, string ordering, UTC arithmetic, real calendar days only, `today` defaulting to the current local date, `due = today + terms`, strict `due < today` overdue test); a module reference for src/money.js, src/store.js, src/customers.js, src/products.js, src/invoices.js and src/report.js with their exact signatures, the exported date helpers and the invoice/line/payment shapes plus the net/tax/total formulas; and a command reference where all twelve commands from design section 7 (`add-customer`, `add-product`, `create`, `add-line`, `issue`, `pay`, `void`, `show`, `list`, `report aging`, `report revenue`, `export`) each have a real invocation and the JSON it prints, followed by the exit-code table (0 success, 1 usage, 2 `{"error":...}`) with verbatim usage and error transcripts, and the `export` CSV shown both as the printed JSON string and as decoded text with the no-trailing-newline rule.

Every example output was transcribed from an actual run of `node bin/invoice.js` against a fresh store in /tmp (never in the repository), in a fixed, reproducible order: two customers, two products (120.00 at 21% tax, 9.99 untaxed), draft invoice 1 with terms 15, two lines (2 x 120.00 at 10% discount -> net 216.00 / tax 45.36, plus 9.99 untaxed), issue on 2026-03-10 -> INV-2026-0001 due 2026-03-25, partial payment 71.35, final payment 200.00 -> paid; invoice 2 for customer 2 (terms 30, issued 2026-02-01 -> due 2026-03-03); invoice 3 created and voided; then show/list/report/export. Usage (exit 1) and error (exit 2) transcripts for `create` without `--customer`, `pay` over the balance, `pay --amount 1.234`, `show --invoice 99`, `void` on a paid invoice, `add-line` on an issued invoice and `issue` without lines were captured the same way and all match the messages in the source. Long JSON values are shown 2-space-indented for readability, with an explicit note that the CLI writes the same value as one compact line and a verbatim single-line `add-customer` example; key order and every money string are exactly as printed.

Also checked that each of the twelve usage-text commands appears in the README (`add-customer` 5 hits, `add-product` 5, `create` 9, `add-line` 4, `issue` 48, `pay` 30, `void` 20, `show` 6, `list` 10, `report aging` 3, `report revenue` 3, `export` 4). Every documented output was produced by running the real CLI in /tmp (e.g. `report aging --today 2026-04-15` printed `{"current":"0.00","days1to30":"0.00","days31to60":"145.20","days61to90":"0.00","over90":"0.00","total":"145.20"}`; `report revenue` printed `[{"month":"2026-02","invoices":1,"total":"145.20"},{"month":"2026-03","invoices":1,"total":"271.35"}]`; `export --invoice 2` printed `"description,quantity,unitPrice,discount,net,tax\nConsulting hour,1,120.00,0,120.00,25.20"`), and error paths were re-verified (`show --invoice 99` -> `{"error":"invoice 99 not found"}` exit 2; `void --invoice 1` on a paid invoice -> `{"error":"cannot void this invoice"}` exit 2; bare `report` -> exit 1 with `report requires a subcommand: aging or revenue`). `git status --short` shows README.md as the only file I added.
decisions: Long JSON results are shown pretty-printed (2-space indent) for readability, with an explicit note that the CLI emits the identical value on one compact line, plus one verbatim single-line example; small values are also identical either way. The README never shows raw cents in any CLI output.

The command reference is written as one ordered walkthrough against a single store so the ids in later examples (invoice 2, invoice 3) are meaningful and reproducible; a reader who runs the commands in order gets exactly the documented output. Fixed dates are supplied via --today so the examples do not depend on the day they are read.

Two long list outputs (the unfiltered `list` and `list --customer 2`) are abbreviated with `...` and an explicit note that each element is the full invoice object shown by `show`; every other example is shown complete.

The module reference documents the additional exports that exist in the code (store's nextNumber/resetStore/ID_KINDS, invoices' currentDate/isValidDate/validateDate/addDays/daysBetween) since the reports and CLI rely on them, while keeping the six required modules as the top-level headings.

`npm test` is documented as `node --test test/*.test.js`, matching the actual package.json script (the glob form is required because Node v26.0.0 rejects a directory argument), not the design's literal `node --test test/`.

projectEvents.summary:
Implemented the invoice lifecycle in src/invoices.js and its node:test suite in test/invoices.test.js; `npm test` runs 96 tests across the repo and exits 0.

src/invoices.js exports createInvoice, addLine, issue, pay, voidInvoice, listInvoices and getInvoice exactly as specified in design §6.3, plus the date helpers the later report/CLI tasks need (currentDate, isValidDate, validateDate, addDays, daysBetween, all UTC-based). createInvoice validates the customer and terms and pushes the documented draft with the design's key order. addLine only mutates drafts, copies the product name into the line description, computes net and line tax rounded half up on the cent, and recomputes subtotal/tax/total/paid/balance from the lines and payments. issue numbers drafts as INV-<year>-<nnnn> using store.nextNumber(year) so voided invoices still consume their number and each year restarts at 0001, and sets issued/due from the (validated, UTC) date arithmetic. pay accepts positive amounts up to the balance on issued invoices, allows partials, and flips the status to paid when paid reaches total. voidInvoice accepts a draft or a payment-free issued invoice and rejects everything else. listInvoices filters on status, customerId and overdue (issued with due < today) and returns invoices sorted by id ascending. Every mutation calls save(); today defaults to the current local date everywhere.

The one deliberate deviation: the design's line formula is scaled. src/money.js roundCents takes whole units and returns cents (roundCents(1.005) === 101, pinned by the existing money tests), while unitPrice and net are integer cents, so the literal `roundCents(unitPrice * quantity * (100 - discount) / 100)` would inflate every line 100x. I used `/ 10000` for both net and tax, which rounds half up on the cent of the cent-valued expression, i.e. what the brief's prose formula says. This is recorded in the decision log with a short comment at the call site.

Tests cover the draft shape and key order, id allocation, terms/customer validation, line totals with discounts and tax rates, the half-up rounding boundaries (9.5 -> 10, 0.5 -> 1, 10.05 -> 10, 6.65 -> 7, 4.5 -> 5), lines rejected on issued/paid/void invoices, description snapshotting, issue without lines, per-year and per-month numbering with voided numbers consumed and a new year restarting, due-date arithmetic across month/year/leap boundaries and terms 0, partial payments, overpayment and malformed amounts, the paid transition, all void rules, list filters and the overdue `due < today` boundary, overdue defaulting to the current date, persistence of every mutation to the raw JSON file (including that a failed operation leaves the file byte-identical), and time-zone stability of the date helpers verified by re-running the arithmetic under four different TZ values.

projectEvents.summary:
Implemented src/report.js (aging and revenue per design §6.4) and test/report.test.js.

aging({ today = currentDate() } = {}) validates `today` with the shared invoices.js validateDate, then walks invoices with status "issued" only (drafts, paid and voided are therefore excluded), buckets each by daysBetween(invoice.due, today) — <= 0 current, 1-30 days1to30, 31-60 days31to60, 61-90 days61to90, > 90 over90 — and adds invoice.balance (not total) into its bucket. total is the sum of the five buckets. Returns exactly { current, days1to30, days31to60, days61to90, over90, total } in cents, key order as specified.

revenue() groups invoices with status "issued" or "paid" by String(invoice.issued).slice(0, 7), producing { month, invoices: count, total: sum of invoice.total } per month, sorted ascending by the month string; returns [] when nothing qualifies. Both functions are pure with respect to the store (read-only, no save()).

test/report.test.js has 14 tests using node:test/node:assert/strict with a fresh temp store per test, all fixtures built through src/invoices.js (never hand-written JSON): empty store; due-after-today and due-today both current; the 0/1/30/31/60/61/90/91-day boundary ladder each with a distinct amount; balance-vs-total (a partially paid issued invoice reports its balance); exclusion of drafts, paid and voided invoices; total equals the sum of the five buckets; today defaulting to the current date; an invalid today throwing; revenue empty; multi-month grouping and sorting; three invoices in one month counted separately; inclusion of paid and exclusion of draft/void; and totals including tax.

Implemented the machine-readable CLI at bin/invoice.js (executable, `#!/usr/bin/env node`) and its test suite test/cli.test.js. The CLI parses `<command> [options] [--data <path>]` itself (no dependencies), opens the store with openStore(dataPath), runs the command, and prints exactly one JSON value on stdout + newline with exit 0. Usage errors (missing/unknown command, unknown or inapplicable option, option without a value, stray positional, missing required option, bad report subcommand) print a usage block on stderr and exit 1. Input/domain errors (invalid option value, money parse failure, missing entity, state violation) print compact `{"error":"<message>"}` on stderr and exit 2; caught module Errors become the exit-2 form. All twelve command forms are implemented (add-customer, add-product, create, add-line, issue, pay, void, show, list, report aging, report revenue, export) with the exact presentation rules from design §7: money flows through one set of present* helpers using formatMoney, so every money field (price, unitPrice, net, tax, subtotal, total, paid, balance, amount, aging buckets, revenue total) is a two-decimal string while quantity/discount/terms/id/status/dates stay plain; the invoice key order is id, number, customerId, status, terms, issued, due, lines, payments, subtotal, tax, total, paid, balance. export builds the RFC-4180 CSV (header description,quantity,unitPrice,discount,net,tax, one row per line, rows joined by "\n", no trailing newline, quoting only when a field holds a comma, quote, CR or LF) and prints it as a single JSON string.

test/cli.test.js (41 tests) spawns the CLI with spawnSync and a temp-dir --data path and covers every command's happy path with exact JSON, the exit-1 usage cases, the exit-2 error cases (bad/negative amount, non-numeric and unknown ids, invalid date, invalid quantity, line on a non-draft, overpayment, void with payments), that successful output contains no raw cents, that --data is honoured (including mid-option placement), that state persists across invocations, that separate --data paths are isolated, and that the file and its nested directory are created on first use (verified via a read-only `report aging`).

One real bug was caught by the tests: export was double-encoding the CSV (JSON.stringify applied in both the command runner and the output helper); the runner now returns the raw CSV text and the single output helper encodes it once.

The file imports nothing from bin/invoice.js or src/ — only node:test, node:assert/strict, child_process, fs, os, path and url — so the CLI is exercised purely through argv, stdout, stderr, exit code and the JSON data file.

Ten tests cover: the full lifecycle (add-customer, two add-product, create --terms 15, add-line with --quantity 3 --discount 10 on a taxed product plus a second untaxed line, exact line/box totals, issue --today 2026-01-15 giving INV-2026-0001 and due 2026-01-30, a partial pay then a final pay flipping the status to paid, and `show` returning exactly the last pay output); per-year numbering restarting at INV-2026-0001/INV-2026-0002/INV-2027-0001; list with --status, --customer, --overdue and --today alone and combined, including the strict `due < today` boundary (not overdue on the due date) and a draft never counting as overdue; report aging across all eight boundaries (0, 1, 30, 31, 60, 61, 90, 91 days past due, built as eight invoices issued with --terms 0 so issue date == due date) plus the exclusion of a fully paid and a draft invoice and the one-day bucket shift; report revenue over two months including a fully paid invoice that still counts and a voided issued invoice plus a draft that do not; export producing the exact CSV text with the no-trailing-newline rule (a quoted description containing a comma, money as two-decimal strings) and stdout equal to JSON.stringify(csv)+"\n"; void of a draft and of an unpaid issued invoice, void rejected after a payment with the invoice left untouched, and line-after-void rejection; unknown command / missing required option / bare `report` exiting 1 with a non-JSON usage block on stderr; and invalid amounts, ids, dates and state exiting 2.
